sections.html:
Start with the Official Records search run by the Broward County Records, Taxes and Treasury Division. It is an Acclaim-based system, and you accept a short disclaimer before you can search.

There are nine ways in: party name (grantor or grantee), book and page, document type, instrument number, case number, consideration range, date recorded, parcel ID, and a simple search with plain-language prompts such as a copy of your deed. If all you need is a quick answer on whether a lien has been recorded against you, the simple search is the fastest place to begin.

sections.h2: How far back the online records go
sections.html:
Everything recorded on or after July 7, 1977 is fully searchable online, and plats and maps can be looked up at any date.

Anything older is harder to reach:

  • March 9, 1972 through July 7, 1977: searchable only by instrument number, book type and book and page range, or record date.
  • Before March 9, 1972: not on the site.

If your Broward house has stayed in one family since the 1960s, plan on an in-person request or a title company search to cover the oldest links in the chain of title.

sections.h2: The recording office and bulk data
sections.html:
Recording sits inside the county's Records, Taxes and Treasury Division, and the phone number for questions is 954-831-4000. Call before you mail a deed so you know the exact amount due.

The division also hands out bulk data: 10 continuous days of Official Records files, with images and index data, at no charge. It lists electronic recording vendors too, for firms that file many documents. One homeowner will rarely use either, though a title company working your closing may well e-record.

sections.h2: What it costs to record a deed
sections.html:
Clerk charges are set by Florida statute, and the lines in this table come from s. 28.24(13). Other charges can be added, so ask the Broward recording office for the final total before you send anything.

sections.h2: Documentary stamp tax on a Broward deed
sections.html:
Broward uses the standard state rate, $0.70 for every $100 of the price and debt transferred. Neighboring Miami-Dade has its own rates, which do not apply here.

Any mortgage on the property is counted as consideration, even when the buyer takes the house without assuming it. Both sides remain liable no matter what the sales contract says about who pays, and leaving a deed unrecorded doesn't make it untaxable.

  • Taxed: warranty, special warranty, quit claim and trustee's deeds, along with deeds in lieu of foreclosure and certificates of title.
  • Exempt: a spousal homestead deed where a mortgage is the only consideration, and a divorce deed for the marital home.
  • Lady bird deeds: in a 2020 advisement the Department of Revenue found one outside the tax on the facts presented, since no present beneficial interest passed.

The Broward County Property Appraiser offers a free Owner Alert service. You subscribe, and it notifies you when the appraiser's office receives a document that changes ownership of your property.

The alert covers ownership changes and nothing else. It suits an owner who is moving out of the area, or heirs holding a vacant inherited house. For questions about recording a deed, adding or removing an owner, or getting copies of recorded documents, use the appraiser's FAQ page: type deed in the questions box and pick the topic closest to your situation.

When ownership changes, assessed value is reset to full market value and the new owner's bill can jump. The Save Our Homes cap a long-time seller enjoyed does not move with the house.

The appraiser doesn't send bills or collect tax. Billing and collection belong to the Broward County Tax Collector, listed by the appraiser at (954) 357-4829 and revenue@browardtax.org. A seller who is buying another Florida home may be able to carry part of the homestead benefit over through portability, as long as the new homestead is established within three years of the first of January in the year the old one was abandoned.

sections.h2: Liens and foreclosures in the records
sections.html:
Search by party name and again by parcel ID. Liens can attach to the person as well as to the land, and one search alone can miss them. A court sale ends with a certificate of title, and ten quiet days confirm it (s. 45.031).

Someone seeking a tax deed has to wait two years from April 1 of the certificate year before applying. The tax collector lists everyone who has to be notified, including mortgagees and contract-for-deed vendees (s. 197.502).

A title company can send the deed electronically through one of the county's listed e-recording vendors. If you are filing by hand, phone 954-831-4000 before you go.

Before filing, verify three details: the grantor's name matches the last recorded deed, the legal description is copied exactly, and the two required witnesses have signed (s. 689.01). Choosing not to file saves nothing, since the stamp tax applies to the deed either way.

  • Pull the parcel ID from the appraiser's site.
  • Get the recording charges and stamp tax in the amounts the office quotes.
  • Write down the instrument number once the deed is recorded. The Broward search supports instrument number lookups, and you will want it for any later copy.

After recording, ask for a conformed or certified copy and store it with your closing papers. Buyers, lenders and later title searches all rely on that recorded instrument.

Try the decedent's name every way it might appear: nicknames, married names, whatever was used on a deed or loan. Watch for mortgages that were paid off but never released. Plats and maps are searchable at every date range, so a lot-line question can be checked there. A personal representative's deed under a probated will is not taxable for stamp tax, and Florida has had no estate tax for deaths after 2004.

Summary administration may fit an estate of $150,000 or less in non-exempt assets, or an owner dead more than two years (s. 735.201). Creditor claims face a cutoff set by s. 733.702. The title insurer will probably want these steps finished before it insures a buyer.

Under s. 702.10 a lender can ask the court for an order to show cause. The hearing then waits for the later of 20 days after the order is served or 45 days after the complaint is served. When a sale has already taken place, the records will show a certificate of title.

Owner-occupied homes are carved out of the quick payment-or-vacate order, and a homestead exemption on the latest roll is a rebuttable presumption of owner occupancy.

If you are behind on a mortgage and thinking of selling, pull your own record first. Knowing what has been filed against the parcel lets you and a buyer, including a cash buyer who skips lender underwriting, plan around the real picture.

faqs.q: Where is the Broward County recording office?
faqs.a: It is the Records, Taxes and Treasury Division of Broward County, reachable at 954-831-4000. The Official Records search has its own site.

faqs.q: Are all Broward deeds searchable online?
faqs.a: No. Documents from July 7, 1977 forward are fully searchable. Records from March 9, 1972 to July 7, 1977 need an instrument number, book and page, or record date, and earlier ones aren't on the site.

faqs.q: What is the Florida deed stamp rate in Broward?
faqs.a: It is $0.70 for every $100 of the price and debt transferred under s. 201.02. Every party is liable, and the tax is collected at filing.

faqs.q: Is there a free alert for deed filings on my Broward home?
faqs.a: Yes. The Broward County Property Appraiser offers Owner Alert, which notifies you when a document changing ownership of your property reaches that office.

faqs.q: Does my assessment cap pass to the buyer?
faqs.a: No. A change of ownership resets assessed value to just value the next first of January. Exceptions cover things like transfers between spouses.
